sections.h2: Where does Upson County sit between Atlanta, Macon and Columbus?
sections.html:
Upson County occupies Georgia's west central region, about equally far from Atlanta, Macon and Columbus. The state legislature established it on December 15, 1824, on land the Creek gave up in the Treaty of Indian Springs of 1821, and many early settlers arrived through the land lottery. It was Georgia's fifty-ninth county, named for a lawyer who had died only four months before.

Thomaston is where county government sits, and The Rock and Yatesville round out the incorporated places. The county reports 326 square miles of land and 592 miles of roads. The Flint River runs unimpeded through the area, and Sprewell Bluff Park, which the county has managed since January 2013, offers trails, cabins, RV sites and an overlook.

Textile mills turned Thomaston into a social and cultural center in the nineteenth century, according to the county's history page, though cotton's hold on the economy had faded by 1900. Houses range from mill-era homes in town to timber and farm tracts outside it.

sections.h2: How big and how settled is Upson County?
sections.html:
Upson County reached an estimated 28,500 residents by mid-2025, a 2.9% gain since 2020. Owners occupy 61.0% of housing units, and a typical owner-held home has a value of $168,700.

sections.h2: Which Upson County office answers which question?
sections.html:
You will find both at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Money owed goes to one door, and questions about value go to the other.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mailing to P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the payoff figure for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mailing to P.O. Box 508, open weekdays through the working day: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an elected office that stands apart from both the assessors and the county commissioners. Statements are addressed to the homeowner and never to the lender, although the office sends mortgage companies a data file. After a change of lender, pass the bill along yourself.

sections.h2: How is an Upson County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
Fair market value, the whole 100% figure, the assessors arrive at, and Upson's FAQ defines assessed value as 40% of that. Exemptions come off the 40%, which leaves the net assessed, or taxable, value. Multiply it by the millage rate to get the bill, with each mill worth one dollar on every $1,000.

Owners may also propose their own value by filing a return during the early-year window that ends April 1. If the assessors disagree, a notice goes out with their figure and the appeal clock starts. A copy of your warranty deed is available from the Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street, Thomaston.

sections.h2: Where do Upson County tax dollars go?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's FAQ lists the uses in plain terms. Property tax pays for the administration of county government and the public school system, for public buildings, bridges and county roads, and for the courts, the jail and law enforcement. It also funds fire protection and public health and sanitation. The FAQ calls this an abbreviated list and refers readers to the Georgia Code for the rest.

The county reports 592 miles of roads across 326 square miles of land. If your bill rose from one year to the next, the county's 2026 notice of increase states the change in mills, so compare it with the rate on your statement.

sections.h2: When do Upson County bills arrive and when are they due?
sections.html:
Real and personal property bills are mailed no later than September 15, and the county FAQ places the due date around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements go out by January 30, and that tax comes due on April 1.

A 2026 notice of property tax increase carried a tentative county rate of 8.244 mills, up 0.391, and listed hearings on August 26 and September 8, 2026. Without the increase the rate would have been no more than 7.853 mills. Your own bill shows the final rate, since the school board and the city set separate ones.

  • The assessed share is 40% of fair market value.
  • Upson's rate is built from separate levies by the Board of Education, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston.
  • The post office's own date stamp proves a timely payment, and a postage meter stamp does not.

sections.h2: What does a late Upson County bill cost in penalties?
sections.html:
Unpaid balances accrue monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% joins it at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20%.

Hardship can justify partial payments, but only if you phone before the due date to arrange them, and interest and penalties keep running on the rest. The office sends a notice of intent with 30 days to pay before it files a FIFA lien on the General Execution Docket. Tax still unpaid 90 days past the due date is open to a lien, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Full payment, fees included, cancels the lien. Buying liens at the counter is not offered.

sections.h2: How do I dispute an Upson County assessment?
sections.html:
Six weeks and three days after the notice date is the cutoff. Four grounds qualify: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. Address the written appeal to the Board of Assessors and say which route you prefer.

The assessors also post a field review notice letting identified representatives walk onto a property in business hours to check its value. The county takes homestead applications from the first of the year through March 31, and they must reach the office by April 1. You must hold the house and live in it on January 1, and a stable owner needs no yearly renewal unless the deed or address changes. Ask at (706) 647-8176 which exemption amounts fit your parcel.

sections.h2: What does an Upson County seller need to do about the bill?
sections.html:
Have the tax commissioner write out a payoff before closing, and see that the closing agent pays it from what the buyer sends. Because the bill carries the name of whoever owned on New Year's Day, an autumn seller should check the settlement sheet to see who covers the current year.

Heirs and landlords should ask about every year they held the house, including any FIFA on file. A lien goes away only when it is paid in full, which is why the buyer's title agent will want the account clear. A cash purchase can settle old balances at closing and hand you the rest, which helps when a house carries back taxes, repairs or tenants.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Upson County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: The number is (706) 647-8931, and the counter is in Suite D-120 at 305 South Hightower Street, Thomaston.

faqs.q: When is Upson County property tax due?
faqs.a: Around November 15 in a typical year, per the county FAQ. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1.

faqs.q: What does late payment cost in Upson County?
faqs.a: Monthly interest equals prime plus 3%. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns at each 120-day mark, stopping at 20%.

faqs.q: What is the Upson County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors and name the appeal method.

faqs.q: Does Upson County mail my bill to my lender?
faqs.a: No. Statements go to the homeowner. Lenders get a data file, and passing the bill along is your job when needed.
